rationale: The workflow already implements the evidence-supported optimizations that apply to it: path-filtered push/pull_request triggers (P-LIT-CHANGE-FILTER), a concurrency group with cancel-in-progress (P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE), and an explicit job timeout of 15 minutes (P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT). No other retrieved pattern fits this workflow: it has a single job (no matrix for fail-fast, job reordering, or build selection), no schedule (no schedule suppression or failing-schedule handling), no Bazel build, no dependency-installation step such as npm ci or go mod download to cache (tools are installed via setup actions), and a single test script (no test selection or prioritization). Adding a cache for helm/kind/kubectl tool downloads is not directly supported by the retrieved evidence, which demonstrates dependency caching with lockfile-keyed inputs (e.g., go.mod/go.sum) rather than setup-action tool binaries, and could introduce cache-related failure modes without measured benefit.
